questions.question_english: What is the primary administrative objective of implementing the 'e-Office' digital application across the Directorate of Education (DoE) and government schools in Delhi?
options_english: To conduct live interactive online classrooms and deliver digital curriculum modules to students.
To monitor daily mid-day meal cooking logs and transport logistics across government schools.
To manage student online admissions and generate centralized district-wise merit lists.
To digitize file movement, eliminate physical paper dependencies, and enhance administrative speed and transparency.
questions.explanation_english:
e-Office is a Mission Mode Project under the Digital India initiative developed by the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and adopted comprehensively by the Government of NCT of Delhi across the Directorate of Education and its field offices.

Key Objectives and Functionalities of e-Office:
1. Digital File Lifecycle (eFile): It transforms physical paper-based file processing into a secure, electronic workflow. Administrative notesheets, correspondences, sanction proposals, service verifications, and approvals are created, digitally signed, and tracked electronically.
2. Transparency and Accountability: Every action, timestamp, and modification is permanently recorded in the system audit trail, eliminating file misplacement, deliberate delays, and unauthorized alterations.
3. Speed and Eco-friendliness: It drastically cuts down the turnaround time for official sanctions and significantly reduces paper consumption, fostering a modern, sustainable governance framework.

Option (A) relates to digital learning platforms like DIKSHA; Option (B) relates to mid-day meal tracking apps; Option (C) refers to the DoE Online Admission Portal. Therefore, Option (D) correctly identifies the core purpose of e-Office.
questions.explanation_hindi:
ई-ऑफिस (e-Office) राष्ट्रीय सूचना विज्ञान केंद्र (NIC) द्वारा विकसित 'डिजिटल इंडिया' कार्यक्रम के तहत एक मिशन मोड परियोजना है, जिसे दिल्ली सरकार द्वारा शिक्षा निदेशालय और उसके अधीनस्थ कार्यालयों में प्रशासनिक सुधार हेतु अनिवार्य किया गया है।

ई-ऑफिस के मुख्य उद्देश्य एवं लाभ:
1. फाइलों का डिजिटल संचलन (eFile): इसके माध्यम से पारंपरिक कागजी फाइलों को इलेक्ट्रॉनिक फाइलों में परिवर्तित किया गया है। प्रशासनिक टिप्पणियां (Notesheets), पत्राचार, वित्तीय स्वीकृतियां और सेवा संबंधी मामलों को ऑनलाइन तैयार, हस्ताक्षरित (डिजिटल हस्ताक्षर) और प्रेषित किया जाता है।
2. पारदर्शिता और उत्तरदायित्व: प्रत्येक फाइल की वास्तविक स्थिति (Live Tracking) और समय का रिकॉर्ड सुरक्षित रहता है, जिससे फाइलों के खोने या जानबूझकर विलंब करने की गुंजाइश समाप्त हो जाती है।
3. त्वरित निर्णय और पर्यावरण संरक्षण: यह आधिकारिक फाइलों के निपटान की गति को कई गुना बढ़ाता है और कागज़ की भारी खपत को रोककर पर्यावरण संरक्षण में योगदान देता है।

विकल्प (A) दीक्षा (DIKSHA) जैसे ई-लर्निंग प्लेटफॉर्म से संबंधित है; विकल्प (B) मिड-डे मील निगरानी प्रणाली है; विकल्प (C) DoE का केंद्रीकृत प्रवेश पोर्टल है। अतः विकल्प (D) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Digitize file movement, reduce paper usage, and improve administrative transparency

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The e-Office application implemented across the Directorate of Education aims to digitize internal file movement, streamline administrative workflows, and reduce paper consumption. By transitioning to digital files, the platform enhances transparency, ensures systematic file tracking, speeds up official decision-making, and maintains accountable record management across educational administrative offices.

questions.question_english: Which document forms the basis for claiming salary and allowances by a DDO from the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO)?
options_english: Salary Bill (GAR-13 or equivalent)
Official Daily Cash Book Register
Consolidated Bank Passbook Account Statement
Approved Annual Budget Estimate Document
questions.explanation_english:
Under the Central Government Accounts (Receipts and Payments) Rules, 1983 and the Civil Accounts Manual issued by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA), Ministry of Finance:

1. Form GAR-13 (Government Accounting Rules Form 13):
Form GAR-13 is the prescribed statutory format for preparing the monthly Pay Bill (Salary Bill) by the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) for all establishment personnel.

2. Key Administrative Role in Salary Claims:
- The DDO prepares the bill based on authenticated attendance rolls, absentee statements, Last Pay Certificates (LPC), increment certificates, and statutory deduction schedules (NPS, GPF, Income Tax, CGEGIS, CGHS/DGHS).
- The Salary Bill (now processed digitally via PFMS / e-HRMS in Form GAR-13 format) contains complete details of basic pay, dearness allowance (DA), house rent allowance (HRA), transport allowance (TA), gross emoluments, deductions, and net payable salary.
- The signed and verified GAR-13 bill is submitted to the Pay and Accounts Office (PAO) for pre-check, audit, and generation of the electronic payment scroll/ECS credit directly into employees' bank accounts.

Other documents:
- Cash Book: Records daily receipts and payments of cash, not the formal claim on PAO.
- Bank Statement: Shows transaction history after payment is processed.
- Budget Estimate: Authorizes expenditure ceiling, but is not an operational claim instrument.

Therefore, Form GAR-13 (Salary Bill) forms the basis for claiming salary and allowances, making Option (A) the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सरकार लेखा (प्राप्ति और संदाय) नियमावली, 1983 [Receipts and Payments Rules, 1983] तथा महालेखा नियंत्रक (CGA) द्वारा जारी सिविल लेखा नियमावली (Civil Accounts Manual) के विधिक प्रावधानों के अनुसार:

1. फॉर्म GAR-13 (Government Accounting Rules Form 13):
फॉर्म GAR-13 एक विधिक निर्धारित प्रारूप है जिसमें आहरण एवं संवितरण अधिकारी (DDO) द्वारा विद्यालय के शैक्षणिक एवं गैर-शैक्षणिक कर्मचारियों के मासिक वेतन बिल (Salary Bill) तैयार किए जाते हैं।

2. वेतन दावे का प्रशासनिक आधार:
- DDO इस बिल को उपस्थिति पंजिका, अनुपस्थिति विवरण (Absentee Statement), अंतिम वेतन प्रमाण पत्र (LPC), वेतन वृद्धि प्रमाण पत्र तथा अनिवार्य कटौतियों (NPS, GPF, आयकर, स्वास्थ्य योजना आदि) के आधार पर तैयार करता है।
- इस बिल में मूल वेतन, महंगाई भत्ता (DA), मकान किराया भत्ता (HRA), परिवहन भत्ता (TA) सहित सकल वेतन (Gross Pay), कटौतियां तथा देय शुद्ध वेतन (Net Pay) का मदवार विवरण होता है।
- वर्तमान में PFMS/e-HRMS प्रणाली के माध्यम से तैयार GAR-13 वेतन बिल को पूर्व-जांच (Pre-check), लेखापरीक्षा तथा सीधे बैंक खातों में भुगतान जारी करने हेतु वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय (PAO) के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किया जाता है।

अन्य विकल्पों का विश्लेषण:
- कैश बुक (रोकड़ बही): दैनिक नकदी लेन-देन दर्ज करती है, यह PAO से दावा करने का बिल नहीं है।
- बैंक पासबुक विवरण: लेन-देन के उपरांत बैंक का वित्तीय विवरण है।
- बजट अनुमान: व्यय की सीमा निर्धारित करता है, किंतु यह वेतन दावे का प्रपत्र नहीं है।

अतः वेतन बिल (फॉर्म GAR-13 या समकक्ष) ही वेतन व भत्तों के दावे का आधार है, जिससे विकल्प (A) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Salary Bill (GAR-13 or equivalent)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The Salary Bill, prepared in Form GAR-13 or equivalent electronic format, serves as the primary formal document presented by the Drawing and Disbursing Officer to the Pay and Accounts Office. It details basic pay, allowances, and statutory deductions to authorize the disbursement of monthly staff salaries from treasury accounts.

questions.question_english: Under the General Financial Rules (GFR) and Central Government Receipt and Payment Rules, which of the following accurately defines 'Contingent Expenditure' (or Contingencies) incurred by a Head of Office / School Principal?
options_english: Recurring monthly expenditure on salaries, special allowances, and honoraria of permanent establishment staff
Incidental and operational expenditure incurred for the day-to-day running and maintenance of an office or school
Major capital expenditure incurred on the acquisition of land and construction of school buildings
Statutory monthly pension and gratuity disbursements payable to retired public servants
questions.explanation_english: Under the General Financial Rules (GFR) and Rule 96 of Central Government Receipt and Payment Rules, 'Contingent Charges' or 'Contingent Expenditure' means and includes all incidental and other expenses which are incurred for the management of an office or for the technical working of a department, but does not include any charges which are classified under some other head of expenditure, such as 'Salaries', 'Wages', 'Travel Expenses', or 'Works / Capital Outlay'. In a government school, contingent expenditure encompasses routine operational costs such as office stationery, postage, internet and telephone charges, electricity/water bills, minor repair of office furniture/equipment, sanitary items, and cleaning supplies necessary for running the school on a day-to-day basis.
questions.explanation_hindi: सामान्य वित्तीय नियमावली (GFR) और रसीद एवं भुगतान नियमावली के नियम 96 के तहत, 'आकस्मिक व्यय' (Contingent Expenditure) का तात्पर्य उन सभी प्रासंगिक (incidental) और परिचालन खर्चों से है जो किसी कार्यालय या विद्यालय के दिन-प्रतिदिन के सामान्य प्रबंधन एवं संचालन के लिए किए जाते हैं। इसमें वेतन (Salaries), भत्ते, यात्रा व्यय अथवा बड़े पूंजीगत निर्माण कार्य (Works/Capital Outlay) शामिल नहीं होते हैं। विद्यालय के संदर्भ में आकस्मिक व्यय में कार्यालय स्टेशनरी, डाक टिकट, दूरभाष एवं इंटरनेट प्रभार, बिजली-पानी के बिल, कार्यालय उपकरणों की छोटी-मोटी मरम्मत, तथा विद्यालय परिसर की सफाई एवं स्वच्छता सामग्री से संबंधित दैनिक परिचालन व्यय शामिल होते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Incidental expenditure for day-to-day office operations

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under General Financial Rules, Contingent Expenditure refers to incidental, administrative, and operational expenses incurred for day-to-day office running. It encompasses routine payments for office stationery, postage, utility bills, equipment maintenance, and minor repairs necessary to maintain regular office operations, excluding establishment salaries, allowances, and major capital infrastructure construction projects.

questions.question_english: Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which specific sub-section mandates private unaided schools to admit at least 25% children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in their entry-level classes?
options_english: Section 12(1)(a)
Section 12(1)(b)
Section 12(1)(c)
Section 12(2)
questions.explanation_english: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 stipulates that an unaided private school not receiving any government aid or grant shall admit in Class I (or pre-school/nursery, if entry-level), to the extent of at least 25% of the strength of that class, children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in the neighborhood and provide free and compulsory elementary education till its completion. Section 12(1)(a) applies to government schools, Section 12(1)(b) applies to aided schools (in proportion to aid received), and Section 12(2) provides the mechanism for reimbursement of per-child expenditure incurred by unaided schools.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 12(1)(c) यह अनिवार्य बनाती है कि कोई भी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त निजी विद्यालय, जिसे सरकार से कोई वित्तीय सहायता या अनुदान प्राप्त नहीं होता, वह अपनी प्रवेश स्तर की कक्षा (कक्षा 1 या पूर्व-प्राथमिक/नर्सरी) में पड़ोस के कमजोर वर्गों और वंचित समूहों के बच्चों को कम से कम 25% सीटों पर अनिवार्य व निःशुल्क प्रवेश देगा। धारा 12(1)(a) सरकारी स्कूलों पर लागू होती है, धारा 12(1)(b) सहायता प्राप्त स्कूलों पर लागू होती है, और धारा 12(2) निजी स्कूलों को प्रति-बच्चा व्यय की सरकारी प्रतिपूर्ति से संबंधित है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Section 12(1)(c)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act 2009 mandates that private unaided schools reserve at least twenty-five percent of entry-level seats for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups. This statutory clause ensures free elementary education in neighborhood private schools, reimbursed by the government per student costs.

questions.question_english: Which formal document is officially issued by the Directorate of Education (DoE), GNCTD, to grant statutory operational recognition to a private unaided school in Delhi?
options_english: Letter of Recognition
Certificate of Accreditation
No Objection Certificate (NOC)
Letter of Intent
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 4 of the Delhi School Education Act, 1973, read with Rules 49, 50, and 51 of the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973, any new school or upgraded school seeking to operate in Delhi must obtain formal recognition from the Directorate of Education, GNCTD. Upon verifying that the school fulfills all mandatory statutory requirements—such as land and building norms, safety certificates, adequacy of classrooms, staff qualifications, minimum pay scales under Section 10(1), and creation of the joint reserve fund—the Directorate issues an official 'Letter of Recognition'. A No Objection Certificate (NOC) is typically issued for affiliation purposes (e.g., to CBSE), but the foundational legal authorization to function as a recognized school in Delhi is the Letter of Recognition.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG) under the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules:
I. Retirement Gratuity is payable to a government employee upon superannuation or retirement.
II. Death Gratuity is payable to the designated nominee or eligible family members if an employee dies while in service.
III. The maximum statutory ceiling for gratuity under 7th CPC recommendations was fixed at ₹20 lakhs (with provision for enhancement upon DA crossing 50%).
IV. An employee must complete a minimum of 20 years of qualifying service to be eligible for any gratuity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II and III only
I and IV only
II, III and IV only
I, II, III and IV
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 50 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 (and corresponding CCS (Pension) Rules, 2021):
1. Statement I is correct: Retirement Gratuity is payable to a government servant who has completed 5 years of qualifying service upon retirement or superannuation. It is calculated at the rate of 1/4th of emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, subject to a maximum of 16.5 times the emoluments.
2. Statement II is correct: Death Gratuity is payable to the nominee or eligible family members if a government employee dies while in service, even if they have completed less than 1 year of service (with varying slabs: 2 times emoluments for <1 year, 6 times for 1–5 years, 12 times for 5–11 years, 20 times for 11–20 years, and up to 33 times for 20+ years).
3. Statement III is correct: Under the 7th Central Pay Commission (7th CPC), the maximum ceiling on gratuity was raised from ₹10 lakhs to ₹20 lakhs, with an automatic provision that whenever Dearness Allowance (DA) rises by 50%, the ceiling enhances by 25% (raising it to ₹25 lakhs).
4. Statement IV is incorrect: An employee requires only 5 years of qualifying service (not 20 years) to become eligible for Retirement Gratuity, and no minimum service is required for Death Gratuity.

Therefore, Statements I, II, and III are correct, making (A) the correct option.

1. कथन I सही है: सेवानिवृत्ति उपदान (Retirement Gratuity) न्यूनतम 5 वर्ष की अर्हक सेवा पूरी करने वाले सरकारी कर्मचारी को अधिवर्षिता या सेवानिवृत्ति पर देय होता है। इसकी गणना सेवा के प्रत्येक पूर्ण छह-माही अवधि के लिए परिलब्धियों के 1/4 भाग के रूप में की जाती है (अधिकतम 16.5 गुना परिलब्धियां)।
2. कथन II सही है: यदि किसी सरकारी कर्मचारी की सेवाकाल के दौरान मृत्यु हो जाती है, तो उसके नामांकित व्यक्ति (nominee) अथवा पात्र परिवार को मृत्यु उपदान देय होता है, भले ही सेवा 1 वर्ष से भी कम क्यों न हो।
3. कथन III सही है: 7वें वेतन आयोग द्वारा ग्रेच्युटी की अधिकतम सीमा ₹10 लाख से बढ़ाकर ₹20 लाख की गई थी, जिसमें यह स्पष्ट प्रावधान था कि महंगाई भत्ता (DA) 50% तक पहुंचने पर यह सीमा 25% बढ़कर ₹25 लाख हो जाएगी।
4. कथन IV गलत है: सेवानिवृत्ति ग्रेच्युटी हेतु न्यूनतम अर्हक सेवा केवल 5 वर्ष है (न कि 20 वर्ष), तथा मृत्यु ग्रेच्युटी के लिए कोई न्यूनतम सेवा अवधि की शर्त नहीं होती।

अतः केवल कथन I, II और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन IV गलत है।

Pension granted upon compulsory retirement imposed as a major disciplinary penalty
Pension granted to the surviving spouse or eligible dependents upon the demise of an in-service employee
Pension granted to a government servant retiring from service upon attaining the statutory age of superannuation
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 35 of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 1972 (corresponding to Rule 35 of CCS Pension Rules, 2021), a 'Superannuation Pension' is granted to a government servant who is retired on his attaining the age of compulsory retirement (superannuation), which is currently 60 years for Central Government and Delhi Administration employees. Key distinctions among civil service pensions include:
1. Superannuation Pension (Rule 35): Granted on attaining official retirement age.
2. Retiring Pension (Rule 36/48/48-A): Granted on voluntary retirement after completing 20 or 30 years of qualifying service.
3. Compulsory Retirement Pension (Rule 40): Sanctioned when an employee is retired compulsorily as a disciplinary penalty by the competent authority.
4. Family Pension (Rule 54): Disbursed to surviving spouse or eligible family members upon the death of a government employee.
Thus, superannuation pension strictly denotes retirement upon reaching statutory superannuation age.

1. अधिवर्षिता पेंशन (नियम 35): आधिकारिक सेवानिवृत्ति आयु प्राप्त करने पर देय।

3. अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति पेंशन (नियम 40): अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई के अंतर्गत दण्डस्वरूप अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्त किए जाने पर स्वीकृत।

questions.explanation_english:
Under the Delhi Government School Admission Guidelines and regulatory orders issued pursuant to Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 and the Delhi School Education Act and Rules (DSEAR) 1973, the Deputy Director of Education (DDE - District) serves as the primary designated appellate and monitoring authority at the district level.

Salient points of this mechanism:
1. Statutory Quota: Private unaided recognized schools in Delhi are mandated to admit at least 25% children belonging to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), Disadvantaged Groups (DG), and Children with Special Needs (CWSN) at entry levels via the DoE's centralized computerized lottery.
2. Grievance Redressal: When parents face arbitrary denial of admission, excessive document demands, or non-compliance by private school managements, complaints are escalated to the DDE (District).
3. Enforcement Powers: The DDE (District) possesses supervisory and quasi-judicial authority to inspect school records, issue show-cause notices, and initiate de-recognition or takeover recommendations under Section 24 of DSEAR 1973 against recalcitrant schools. Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.question_english: Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, no child admitted to a school shall be held back in any class or expelled from school until the completion of elementary education. Which section of the Act mandates this provision?
options_english: Section 16
Section 21
Section 29
Section 30
questions.explanation_english:
Section 16 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 specifically embodies the statutory prohibition against detention and expulsion during elementary education. It unequivocally states: 'No child admitted in a school shall be held back in any class or expelled from school till the completion of elementary education' (Classes I to VIII).

Key Statutory Framework and Educational Implications:
1. Non-Detention Policy & Child Rights: The policy was designed to prevent dropouts caused by the stigma, humiliation, and psychological trauma of failing, ensuring continuous learning and retention across government and recognized private schools.
2. Legislative Evolution: The RTE (Amendment) Act, 2019 amended Section 16 to allow states to hold regular examinations in Class V and Class VIII. If a child fails, they are given remedial teaching and a re-examination within two months. Even if the state decides not to hold back, the prohibition on expulsion remains absolute—no child can be expelled from school before completing elementary education under any circumstances.
3. Analysis of Other Options:
- Section 21: Pertains to the mandatory constitution, composition, and functions of the School Management Committee (SMC).
- Section 29: Deals with the curriculum and evaluation procedure, emphasizing continuous and comprehensive evaluation (CCE) and child-centered learning.
- Section 30: Prohibits requiring any child to pass any board examination until the completion of elementary education, and mandates the award of an elementary education completion certificate.

Therefore, Section 16 is the correct section mandating no-detention and no-expulsion.

questions.explanation_english:
Under the General Financial Rules (GFR), 2017 and Delhi Financial Rules (DFR), the Head of Office (HoO) / Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) in a school plays a crucial role in budget formulation:

1. **Compilation of Budget Estimates (BE) and Revised Estimates (RE)**:
   - The DDO evaluates expenditure trends from previous financial years, analyzes existing liabilities (staff salaries, increments, contractual payments, utility bills), and forecasts upcoming institutional requirements (maintenance, lab upgrades, annual school functions, Vidyalaya Kalyan Samiti - VKS funds, examination expenses).
2. **Head-wise Allocation**:
   - Prepares itemized budget forecasts under specific major/minor heads: Revenue (Salaries, Medical reimbursements, LTC, Office Expenses - OE) and Capital works.
3. **Timely Submission & Avoiding Under/Over Estimation**:
   - Submits draft estimates to the controlling officer (Deputy Director of Education - DDE / Finance Branch) well within prescribed deadlines to prevent rushed spending at the end of the fiscal year (March rush) or surrender of essential public funds.

questions.question_english: Under the provisions of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972, which specific rule empowers the competent leave sanctioning authority to convert one kind of leave retrospectively into another kind?
options_english: Rule 10
Rule 14
Rule 21
Rule 39
questions.explanation_english:
Rule 10 of the Central Civil Services (Leave) Rules, 1972 specifically governs the 'Commutation / Conversion of one kind of leave into another'.

Key legal and administrative provisions of Rule 10:
1. Retrospective Conversion: At the request of a government servant, the authority that granted them leave or the authority competent to grant leave may convert any kind of leave (including extraordinary leave without pay) retrospectively into leave of a different kind that was admissible to the employee at the time the leave was originally applied for and taken.
2. Discretionary Nature: Conversion of leave cannot be claimed as a matter of absolute legal right by the government servant; it rests entirely within the administrative discretion of the competent leave sanctioning authority, taking into account public interest and applicant eligibility.
3. Prescribed Timeframe: The employee must submit a written representation for retrospective conversion within a reasonable timeframe (ordinarily within 30 days of resuming duty).
4. Related Leave Rules: Rule 14 relates to maximum continuous leave; Rule 21 governs commencement and termination of leave; Rule 39 deals with encashment of leave upon superannuation or quitting service.

In Delhi Government educational administration, school principals and Heads of School (HoS) frequently apply Rule 10 to regularize absence periods of teachers—for example, converting extraordinary leave (EOL) into Half Pay Leave (HPL) or Commuted Leave upon subsequent production of valid medical certificates.
questions.explanation_hindi:

नियम 10 के प्रमुख बिंदु:
1. पूर्वव्यापी रूपांतरण: सरकारी कर्मचारी के लिखित अनुरोध पर, सक्षम अवकाश स्वीकृति प्राधिकारी कर्मचारी द्वारा पूर्व में लिए गए किसी भी प्रकार के अवकाश (असाधारण/अवैतनिक अवकाश सहित) को पूर्वव्यापी प्रभाव (भूतलक्षी प्रभाव) से किसी अन्य अनुमेय अवकाश (जैसे उपार्जित अवकाश या अर्ध-वेतन अवकाश) में परिवर्तित कर सकता है, बशर्ते वह अवकाश उस समय कर्मचारी के खाते में देय था।
2. अधिकार के रूप में दावा नहीं: अवकाश का रूपांतरण कर्मचारी के अधिकार के रूप में दावा नहीं किया जा सकता, यह सक्षम प्राधिकारी के प्रशासनिक स्वविवेक पर निर्भर करता है।
3. समय-सीमा: कर्मचारी को ड्यूटी पर पुनः उपस्थित होने के 30 दिनों के भीतर रूपांतरण हेतु औपचारिक आवेदन करना आवश्यक होता है।
4. अन्य नियम: नियम 14 अधिकतम अवकाश अवधि, नियम 21 अवकाश के प्रारंभ और समाप्ति, तथा नियम 39 सेवानिवृत्ति पर अवकाश के नकदीकरण (Leave Encashment) से संबंधित है।

दिल्ली शिक्षा निदेशालय (DoE) के अंतर्गत विद्यालय प्रमुख (HoS/Principal) शिक्षकों के असाधारण अवकाश या मेडिकल लीव के मामलों को नियमित (regularize) करने के लिए नियम 10 का प्रयोग करते हैं।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following steps involved in departmental disciplinary proceedings for the imposition of a major penalty under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965:
I. Issue of formal Charge Sheet (Articles of Charge)
II. Consideration of the Inquiry Report by the Disciplinary Authority
III. Appointment of the Inquiry Officer (Inquiring Authority)
IV. Submission of written statement of defense by the charged officer
Which of the following represents the correct chronological sequence?
options_english: I, III, IV, II
I, IV, III, II
III, I, IV, II
I, IV, II, III
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 14 of the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965, the procedure for imposing major penalties (dismissal, removal, compulsory retirement, reduction to lower grade/rank) follows a strict statutory sequence mandated by the principles of natural justice and Article 311 of the Constitution:

Step-by-Step Chronology:
1. Step I (Rule 14(3)): The Disciplinary Authority draws up and delivers the formal charge sheet (Articles of Charge, Statement of Imputations of misconduct, List of Documents, and List of Witnesses) to the charged officer.
2. Step IV (Rule 14(4)): The charged government servant is given a specified time (ordinarily 15 days) to submit a written statement of defense admitting or denying the charges.
3. Step III (Rule 14(5)): If the charged officer denies the charges or fails to submit a defense statement, the Disciplinary Authority appoints an Inquiring Authority (Inquiry Officer) and a Presenting Officer to inquire into the charges.
4. Step II (Rule 15): After conclusion of the formal inquiry, the Inquiry Officer submits the Inquiry Report. A copy is served to the charged employee for representation within 15 days, after which the Disciplinary Authority considers the Inquiry Report, findings, and representation before passing final orders.

Thus, the correct sequence is I -> IV -> III -> II (Option B).
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण एवं अपील) नियम, 1965 के नियम 14 तथा भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 311 के अंतर्गत बड़े दंड (जैसे बर्खास्तगी, निष्कासन, अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति या पदावनति) हेतु अनुशासनात्मक कार्यवाही एक निश्चित कानूनी क्रम में संचालित की जाती है:

कालानुक्रमिक चरण:
1. चरण I (नियम 14(3)): अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी द्वारा आरोपित कर्मचारी को औपचारिक आरोप-पत्र (आरोप के अनुच्छेद, कदाचार के अभिकथन, दस्तावेजों की सूची और गवाहों की सूची) जारी कर तामील कराया जाता है।
2. चरण IV (नियम 14(4)): आरोपित अधिकारी को आरोपों को स्वीकार या अस्वीकार करते हुए अपना लिखित प्रतिवाद (बचाव पक्ष का बयान) प्रस्तुत करने के लिए समय दिया जाता है।
3. चरण III (नियम 14(5)): यदि आरोपित अधिकारी आरोपों से इनकार करता है, तो अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी आरोपों की विस्तृत जांच हेतु जांच अधिकारी (Inquiry Officer) तथा प्रस्तुति अधिकारी (Presenting Officer) नियुक्त करता है।
4. चरण II (नियम 15): जांच अधिकारी द्वारा जांच पूरी कर रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करने के पश्चात, उसकी प्रति आरोपित अधिकारी को अभ्यावेदन हेतु दी जाती है, और अंत में अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी जांच रिपोर्ट व अभ्यावेदन पर विचार कर अंतिम आदेश पारित करता है।

अतः सही कालानुक्रम I -> IV -> III -> II है (विकल्प B)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, IV, III, II

questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 141 of the Delhi School Education Rules (DSER), 1973 and Section 14 of the RTE Act, 2009, read with DoE admission circulars, the permissible documents for verifying a child's date of birth are: (1) An official birth certificate issued by the Registrar of Births and Deaths or the Municipal Corporation/local local self-government; (2) Hospital/Auxiliary Nurse and Midwife (ANM) register record generated at the time of delivery; (3) Anganwadi record; or (4) A declaration/undertaking of age by the parents or guardians sworn before a competent authority or submitted as a self-declaration. questions.explanation_english: Fundamental Rule 22(I)(a)(1) governs the fixation of pay of a government servant upon appointment or promotion to a higher post that carries duties and responsibilities of greater importance than those attaching to the post held earlier. Under this rule, the employee's initial pay in the promotional pay scale/pay matrix level is fixed after adding one notional increment to their pay in the feeder post, and then placing their pay at the equal or next higher cell in the promotional level. In contrast, FR 22(I)(a)(2) applies to appointments where the new post does not involve duties of greater importance (where no promotional increment is given, and pay is simply fixed at the same stage or next higher stage).
questions.explanation_hindi: मूल नियम 22(I)(a)(1) [FR 22(I)(a)(1)] उस स्थिति में वेतन निर्धारण को नियंत्रित करता है जब किसी सरकारी कर्मचारी की पदोन्नति किसी ऐसे उच्च पद पर होती है जिसमें पूर्व पद की तुलना में अधिक महत्वपूर्ण कर्तव्य और जिम्मेदारियां शामिल होती हैं। इस नियम के तहत, निचले पद के वेतन में पहले एक काल्पनिक वेतन वृद्धि (Notional Increment) जोड़ी जाती है, और फिर पदोन्नत पद के पे-मैट्रिक्स स्तर में समान या ठीक अगले उच्च सेल (Cell) में वेतन निर्धारित किया जाता है। FR 22(I)(a)(2) उन मामलों में लागू होता है जहां जिम्मेदारियां अधिक महत्वपूर्ण नहीं होती हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) FR 22(I)(a)(1)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: When a government employee is promoted to a post carrying duties of higher responsibility, pay fixation is performed under Fundamental Rule 22(I)(a)(1). Under this rule, one notional increment is added to the pay in the lower level, and pay is then fixed at the immediate higher cell in the promoted level.

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, read with the Delhi Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Rules, 2011, and relevant Directorate of Education (DoE) admission circulars:

1. Legal Residency Requirement:
The reservation of 25% seats in entry-level classes (Nursery, KG, Class I) of recognized private unaided schools for children belonging to Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Disadvantaged Groups (DG) within the NCT of Delhi is a state-funded statutory scheme. Therefore, eligibility is strictly restricted to bona fide residents of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

2. Competent Authority for Income Certification:
Under Delhi RTE rules and revenue department notifications, the income certificate (certifying that total annual family income from all sources does not exceed the notified threshold, currently ₹1 Lakh / ₹2.5 Lakh as notified by GNCTD) must be issued exclusively by a competent revenue officer of GNCT of Delhi (e.g., Sub-Divisional Magistrate / Executive Magistrate / Tehsildar of the concerned revenue district of Delhi). Certificates issued by authorities of neighboring states (such as Haryana or Uttar Pradesh) are invalid for claiming EWS admission in Delhi schools.

3. Relationship between Assertion and Reason:
- Assertion (A) is TRUE: Schools must scrutinize and ensure that the income certificate submitted has been issued by a designated revenue authority of the GNCT of Delhi.
- Reason (R) is TRUE: The EWS quota entitlement in Delhi schools is statutorily restricted to residents of NCT of Delhi holding valid local certificates.
- Furthermore, Reason (R) directly explains why Assertion (A) is mandated: because the quota is localized to Delhi residents, the documentation proving financial weakness and residence must originate from Delhi's competent revenue administration.

Hence, both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A, making Option (A) the correct answer.

2. सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा जारी आय प्रमाण पत्र:
दिल्ली सरकार के नियमों के अनुसार EWS श्रेणी के तहत वार्षिक पारिवारिक आय सीमा का प्रमाण पत्र केवल GNCTD के सक्षम राजस्व प्राधिकारी (उप-मंडल दंडाधिकारी - SDM / तहसीलदार / कार्यकारी मजिस्ट्रेट) द्वारा जारी डिजिटल रूप से सत्यापित प्रमाण पत्र ही मान्य होता है। अन्य राज्यों (जैसे उत्तर प्रदेश, हरियाणा आदि) के प्राधिकारियों द्वारा जारी प्रमाण पत्र दिल्ली में EWS प्रवेश के लिए स्वीकार्य नहीं हैं।

3. अभिकथन और कारण का संबंध:

questions.question_english: A teacher applies for a transfer on medical grounds. According to the comprehensive transfer policy of the Directorate of Education (DoE), GNCTD, such applications are processed through:
options_english: A physical paper dossier routed directly to the Lieutenant Governor's Secretariat
A grievance petition submitted to the district-level grievance redressal cell
A direct legal appeal filed before the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)
An online module on the edudel portal verified and forwarded by the Head of School (HoS)
questions.explanation_english: Under the Comprehensive Online Transfer Policy formulated by the Directorate of Education (DoE), GNCTD, all categories of teacher transfer applications—including routine annual transfers, mutual transfers, and applications on medical or compassionate grounds—must be processed exclusively through the dedicated online transfer module on the MIS portal (edudel.nic.in). Teachers seeking transfer on medical grounds must upload certified medical documents issued by an authorized government hospital medical board. The Head of School (Principal/Vice-Principal) is statutorily mandated to verify the service particulars, leave history, and genuineness of medical records on the portal before forwarding the application online to the concerned Regional Director / DDE. Offline paper representations and direct submissions to higher authorities are strictly prohibited to ensure objectivity, transparency, and equity.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा निदेशालय (GNCTD) की व्यापक ऑनलाइन स्थानांतरण नीति के अनुसार, शिक्षकों के सभी प्रकार के स्थानांतरण आवेदन—चाहे वे सामान्य वार्षिक स्थानांतरण हों, पारस्परिक (mutual) स्थानांतरण हों अथवा गंभीर चिकित्सीय/अनुकंपा के आधार पर हों—अनिवार्य रूप से शिक्षा विभाग के एमआईएस पोर्टल (edudel.nic.in) पर विकसित ऑनलाइन ट्रांसफर मॉड्यूल के माध्यम से ही प्रस्तुत और संसाधित किए जाते हैं। चिकित्सीय आधार पर स्थानांतरण चाहने वाले शिक्षकों को अधिकृत सरकारी मेडिकल बोर्ड द्वारा जारी प्रमाण पत्र ऑनलाइन अपलोड करना होता है। विद्यालय प्रमुख (Head of School - HoS) द्वारा पोर्टल पर शिक्षक के सेवा विवरण, अवकाश इतिहास और संलग्न चिकित्सा प्रमाण पत्रों का भौतिक व अभिलेखीय सत्यापन किया जाता है, जिसके उपरांत आवेदन को ऑनलाइन शिक्षा उपनिदेशक/क्षेत्रीय निदेशक को अग्रेषित किया जाता है। निष्पक्षता एवं पारदर्शिता बनाए रखने हेतु किसी भी प्रकार के ऑफलाइन अथवा कागजी अभ्यावेदन स्वीकार नहीं किए जाते हैं।

questions.question_english: Under the statutory framework of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, the elaborate procedure for conducting a formal departmental inquiry under Rule 14 is legally mandatory prior to imposing which category of sanctions?
options_english: Censure
Withholding of promotion for a specified tenure
Recovery from pay of pecuniary loss caused to the State
Major penalties (clauses v to ix of Rule 11)
questions.explanation_english:
Under the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, disciplinary proceedings are bifurcated based on the gravity of the penalty:

1. Rule 14 (Procedure for imposing Major Penalties): Imposing any major penalty—such as reduction in rank, compulsory retirement, removal, or dismissal (Rule 11, clauses v to ix)—mandates a formal departmental inquiry in strict compliance with Article 311(2) of the Constitution of India and principles of natural justice. This involves framing formal charges, presenting evidence, cross-examination of witnesses, and an Inquiry Report by an appointed Inquiry Officer.
2. Rule 16 (Procedure for imposing Minor Penalties): Minor penalties (censure, withholding of promotion, recovery of pecuniary loss, withholding of increments without cumulative effect) generally require only a memorandum of charges, representation by the employee, and a reasoned order by the disciplinary authority, without holding a mandatory oral inquiry (unless the disciplinary authority decides otherwise or in special circumstances involving cumulative effects).

Hence, Rule 14 is mandatory for imposing Major Penalties (Option D).
questions.explanation_hindi:
केंद्रीय सिविल सेवा (वर्गीकरण, नियंत्रण एवं अपील) नियमावली, 1965 के तहत अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई की प्रक्रिया को दो श्रेणियों में बांटा गया है:

1. नियम 14 (दीर्घ शास्तियां अधिरोपित करने की प्रक्रिया): संविधान के अनुच्छेद 311(2) तथा प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांतों के अनुसार, किसी भी कर्मचारी पर दीर्घ शास्ति (जैसे पद अवनति, अनिवार्य सेवानिवृत्ति, सेवा से हटाया जाना या बर्खास्तगी) लगाने से पूर्व नियम 14 के तहत औपचारिक विभागीय जांच (Oral Departmental Inquiry) संचालित करना अनिवार्य है। इसमें आरोप पत्र जारी करना, साक्ष्य प्रस्तुत करना, गवाहों की जिरह और जांच अधिकारी (IO) द्वारा जांच रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करना शामिल है।
2. नियम 16 (लघु शास्तियां अधिरोपित करने की प्रक्रिया): परिनिंदा, पदोन्नति रोकना, वेतन से वित्तीय नुकसान की वसूली आदि जैसी लघु शास्तियों हेतु नियम 16 के तहत केवल कर्मचारी को लिखित अभ्यावेदन का अवसर देना पर्याप्त होता है, जिसमें पूर्ण मौखिक जांच अनिवार्य नहीं होती (जब तक कि विशेष परिस्थिति न हो)।

अतः नियम 14 के तहत जांच केवल दीर्घ शास्तियों (Major Penalties) के लिए अनिवार्य है (विकल्प D)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Major penalties

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Rule 14 of the Central Civil Services Classification, Control and Appeal Rules 1965 prescribes the detailed procedure for conducting a formal inquiry before imposing major penalties. Such inquiries are mandatory to afford the accused employee a reasonable opportunity to defend against specific charges, ensuring natural justice throughout administrative disciplinary proceedings.

questions.question_english: In accordance with the provisions of the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973, who serves as the designated disciplinary authority for employees of a recognized private unaided school?
options_english: The Director of Education, Government of NCT of Delhi
The Managing Committee of the school
The general School Management Committee (SMC) constituted under RTE
The concerned District Deputy Director of Education (DDE)
questions.explanation_english: Under Rule 118 and Rule 120 of the Delhi School Education Rules, 1973 (DSER 1973), read with Section 8 of the DSEA 1973, the Managing Committee (MC) of a recognized private unaided school is the designated disciplinary authority empowered to institute disciplinary proceedings, frame charge-sheets, and impose minor or major penalties against its employees (teachers and staff). While the Managing Committee conducts the inquiry and imposes penalties following the principles of natural justice and statutory procedures, Section 8(2) traditionally required prior approval of the Director of Education for major penalties like dismissal or termination (as shaped by key judicial precedents including TMA Pai Foundation and Raj Kumar v. Director of Education).
questions.explanation_hindi: दिल्ली स्कूल शिक्षा नियम, 1973 के नियम 118 और नियम 120 तथा DSEA 1973 की धारा 8 के तहत, किसी मान्यता प्राप्त गैर-सहायता प्राप्त निजी विद्यालय के कर्मचारियों (शिक्षकों और गैर-शिक्षण कर्मचारियों) के लिए स्कूल की 'प्रबंध समिति' (Managing Committee) ही नामित अनुशासनात्मक प्राधिकारी होती है। प्रबंध समिति के पास अनुशासनात्मक जांच शुरू करने, आरोप-पत्र जारी करने और वैधानिक प्रक्रियाओं का पालन करते हुए लघु अथवा दीर्घ शास्ति (दंड) लगाने की प्रशासनिक शक्तियां होती हैं। प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांतों और वैधानिक नियमों का अनुपालन सुनिश्चित करना प्रबंध समिति का दायित्व है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The Managing Committee of the school

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: According to the Delhi School Education Rules 1973, the Managing Committee of a recognized private unaided school functions as the designated disciplinary authority for its employees. It possesses administrative powers to initiate disciplinary proceedings, issue charge sheets, and impose penalties in compliance with statutory procedure and approval rules.
